description.narrative: The initiative “Greening with Women: From Waste to Livelihoods”, led by the ESE and co-implemented by Grac Technology Joint Stock Company in collaboration with the Women’s Union of Hiep Thanh Ward, aims to establish and pilot the Women’s Modern Waste Collection Club, with a vision toward forming a Women-led Environmental Cooperative. The model aims to address the following key issues: - Enhancing the capacity of women engaged in traditional scrap collecting, including informal waste pickers and scrap dealers, through the establishment of a Women’s Modern Waste Collection Club. This serves as a foundation for a future Women-led Environmental Cooperative, whose core members will be trained in operational management, finance, communication, and partner engagement to ensure the model’s sustainability. - Implementing waste collection and traceability for recyclable materials through the Grac application platform, creating a basis for integrating collectors into the green EPR ecosystem (collectors – scrap dealers – recyclers – producers fulfilling their EPR obligations). This contributes to building a transparent and efficient recycling value chain and creating sustainable employment opportunities for women. - Raising awareness among local residents regarding household solid waste separation at source and waste-for-gifts exchange activities within the ward. - Providing traceability data for local authorities to support waste monitoring, thereby contributing to the implementation of policies on waste segregation at source, waste recycling, and plastic waste reduction.

participating-org.narrative: Center Environmental Safety Problem Response (hereinafter referred to as ESE) was established under Decision No. 02/QĐ-GRECO dated April 7, 2017, by Greco Development Joint Stock Company and was granted its initial Science and Technology Operation Registration Certificate by the Department of Science and Technology of Ho Chi Minh City on May 24, 2017. The registration was subsequently amendedfor the second time on April 22, 2019, covering the following scientific and technological fields: - Scientific research and technological development in waste management and treatment (solid, liquid, gaseous); clean production and recycling technologies; environmental recovery and restoration technologies; lifecycle assessment technologies; environmental monitoring technologies; pollution control and treatment technologies; occupational safety; labor hygiene; and environmental sanitation. - Scientific and technological services, including consultancy, technology transfer, training, and professional capacity building in the registered fields (certification is only permitted when legally authorized by the competent State authority). - Domestic and international cooperation in the registered fields in accordance with applicable legal regulations.
